function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Here’s a quick rundown of the most common ways people get fresh‑baked or pre‑made cakes delivered—plus a few extra tricks so your order turns out exactly how you’d like: | Category | Typical Options | Why You Might Choose Them | |----------|-----------------|---------------------------| | **Local Bakeries** | • Your neighborhood shop
• Specialty artisan bakers (e.g., “Baker & Co.”)
• Farm‑to‑table cafés | *Freshness* – usually baked within hours.
*Personal touch* – many offer custom designs or flavor tweaks. | | **National Chains / Supermarkets** | • Costco, Trader Joe’s, Whole Foods (in‑store or curbside)
• Walmart Grocery Delivery | *Convenience* – one-stop shopping.
*Price point* – often cheaper than boutique bakeries. | | **Online Food Marketplaces** | • DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub, Postmates
• Instacart (for store‑picked items) | *Speed* – same‑day delivery in many cities.
*Variety* – choose from multiple vendors at once. | | **Specialty Cake Makers** | • Online sites like **Cake Boss**, **Bakeology**, **Cakes.com**
• Local “custom cake” studios that ship nationwide | *Customization* – unique themes, flavors, sizes.
*Professional finish* – high‑quality decorations. | | **Subscription Boxes** | • **Goldbelly** (regional specialties shipped across the U.S.)
• Monthly dessert clubs (e.g., **Dessert Club**) | *Discovery* – try regional favorites without traveling.
*Gift idea* – great for birthdays or anniversaries. | | **DIY Kits + Delivery** | • Baking kits from **Amazon**, **Boxed**, or **Cratejoy** | *Hands‑on fun* – bake yourself while getting all ingredients ready-made. | ### How to Pick the Right Option 1. **Know Your Location** - Search “[city] bakeries near me” → Google Maps shows top-rated spots with photos/reviews. - Check Yelp or TripAdvisor for recent customer experiences. 2. **Define Your Needs** - **Flavor**: Classic vanilla/chocolate vs. exotic (matcha, salted caramel). - **Dietary Restrictions**: Gluten‑free, vegan, keto, nut‑free. - **Size & Shape**: Standard round, sheet, tiered wedding cake, cupcakes. 3. **Timing Matters** - For events, place orders **at least 48–72 hrs ahead** unless you’re buying a simple store‑purchased cake. - Same‑day deliveries work fine for last‑minute needs—but check cut‑off windows. 4. **Check Packaging & Shipping Policies** - Does the vendor use insulated bags or temperature‑controlled containers? - Are there additional fees for fragile or oversized orders? 5. **Read Reviews About Delivery Experience** - Look specifically for comments on arrival condition (“cake arrived intact”) rather than just taste. --- #### Quick Starter Checklist - [ ] Identify event date/time. - [ ] Decide between freshly baked vs. pre‑made. - [ ] List any allergies/dietary rules. - [ ] Set a rough price range ($20–$200+ depending on size). - [ ] Browse two or three providers (local + online). - [ ] Place order with clear instructions (delivery address, contact phone). If you let me know your zip code or city, I can pull up a handful of highly rated bakeries nearby—or suggest a particular style of cake that fits your occasion!
